voice.text: Two things from our kitchen. The wooden chair, [pause] and the glass cup. One of them needed a <emphasis>plant</emphasis> to exist. Which one? Tap your guess.

Look around the kitchen. The wooden table — that was a <emphasis>tree</emphasis>. Your cotton shirt — a fluffy cotton plant. Bread — made from wheat. The apple — straight off a tree. Even paper — a tree again! [pause] Plant things are <emphasis>everywhere.</emphasis>
Plants give a quieter gift too. Their green leaves <emphasis>freshen the air we breathe.</emphasis> [pause] Take a deep breath — thank a plant!
And the animals? The bird builds her nest in the oak. The squirrel eats its acorns. The caterpillar munches the leaves. [pause] Plants are <emphasis>home and dinner</emphasis>, both at once.

Here is a plant secret hiding underground: <emphasis>roots.</emphasis> Two hills in the rain. The planted hill — the roots grip the soil like tiny hands, and the hill stays. [pause] The bare hill — no roots, and the rain washes the soil away, down and gone.

Things to use, fresh air, homes, food, and soil held tight. [pause] That is why we plant new trees when we cut, and keep plants growing on the land. If we cut every tree and planted nothing, we would lose all those gifts at once.
Look at each thing. Did it come from a plant, or not? [pause] Drag the card, or tap a button. Careful — some are tricky!
